passages.text: Woe to those who enact unjust statutes and issue oppressive decrees, to deprive the poor of fair treatment and withhold justice from the oppressed of My people, to make widows their prey and orphans their plunder.
passages.sermon:
God warns those who make laws.
These people write evil rules.
They create trouble with their decrees.
They twist justice away from the poor.
They steal fair judgment from the needy among God’s people.
They take widows as their prey.
They plunder orphans.
passages.original: ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי־ אָ֑וֶן וּֽמְכַתְּבִ֥ים עָמָ֖ל כִּתֵּֽבוּ׃ לְהַטּ֤וֹת מִדִּין֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְלִגְזֹ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיֵּ֣י עַמִּ֑י לִהְי֤וֹת אַלְמָנוֹת֙ שְׁלָלָ֔ם וְאֶת־ יְתוֹמִ֖ים יָבֹֽזּוּ׃

passages.text: What will you do on the day of reckoning when devastation comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
passages.sermon:
God warns the people of Israel.
He asks them about the coming day of judgment.
He says a day of reckoning will arrive.
Destruction will come from a distant place.
He asks, "What will you do then?"
He asks, "To whom will you run for help?"
He asks, "Where will you put your riches?"
God shows that no one can escape His judgment.
No wealth or power can save them.
passages.original: וּמַֽה־ תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם פְּקֻדָּ֔ה וּלְשׁוֹאָ֖ה מִמֶּרְחָ֣ק תָּב֑וֹא עַל־ מִי֙ תָּנ֣וּסוּ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה וְאָ֥נָה תַעַזְב֖וּ כְּבוֹדְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
passages.sermon:
God warns those who do evil.
\r\nThey will have no escape.
\r\nThey will crouch among the captives.
\r\nThey will fall among the slain.
\r\nGod’s anger will not turn away.
\r\nHis hand will still be raised against them.
passages.original: בִּלְתִּ֤י כָרַע֙ תַּ֣חַת אַסִּ֔יר וְתַ֥חַת הֲרוּגִ֖ים יִפֹּ֑לוּ בְּכָל־ זֹאת֙ לֹא־ שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My wrath.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Assyria.
Assyria is a nation.
God uses Assyria as a tool.
God calls Assyria the rod of His anger.
God says His anger is like a rod in Assyria’s hand.
God says the staff in Assyria’s hand is His wrath.
God warns Assyria with sorrow.
passages.original: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑י וּמַטֶּה־ ה֥וּא בְיָדָ֖ם זַעְמִֽי׃

passages.text: I will send him against a godless nation; I will dispatch him against a people destined for My rage, to take spoils and seize plunder, and to trample them down like clay in the streets.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God describes Assyria.
Assyria is the rod of God's anger.
God will send Assyria against a godless nation.
God will command Assyria against a people who face His wrath.
Assyria will take their spoils.
Assyria will seize their plunder.
Assyria will trample them down.
They will be like clay in the streets under Assyria's feet.
passages.original: בְּג֤וֹי חָנֵף֙ אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ וְעַל־ עַ֥ם עֶבְרָתִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֔ז וּלְשִׂימוֹ מִרְמָ֖ס כְּחֹ֥מֶר חוּצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But this is not his intention; this is not his plan. For it is in his heart to destroy and cut off many nations.
passages.sermon:
Assyria is the subject.
Assyria acts as the rod of God's anger.
Assyria does not intend to serve God's purpose.
Assyria does not plan to carry out God's will.
Assyria has a different purpose in his heart.
Assyria wants to destroy.
Assyria wants to cut off many nations.
passages.original: וְהוּא֙ לֹא־ כֵ֣ן יְדַמֶּ֔ה וּלְבָב֖וֹ לֹא־ כֵ֣ן יַחְשֹׁ֑ב כִּ֚י לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד בִּלְבָב֔וֹ וּלְהַכְרִ֥ית גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א מְעָֽט׃

passages.text: “Are not all my commanders kings?” he says.
passages.sermon: The king of Assyria speaks.\r\nHe says, “All my commanders are kings.”
passages.original: כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א שָׂרַ֛י יַחְדָּ֖ו מְלָכִֽים׃

passages.text: “Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks with pride.
He compares the cities he has conquered.
He says, “Calno is like Carchemish.”
He says, “Hamath is like Arpad.”
He says, “Samaria is like Damascus.”
He treats all these cities as the same.
He believes he has power over them all.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֥א כְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ כַּלְנ֑וֹ אִם־ לֹ֤א כְאַרְפַּד֙ חֲמָ֔ת אִם־ לֹ֥א כְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: As my hand seized the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria, and as I have done to Samaria and its idols, will I not also do to Jerusalem and her idols?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks with pride.
He says his hand seized kingdoms that worship idols.
These kingdoms had many images and idols.
Their idols were greater than those in Jerusalem and Samaria.
He says he conquered Samaria and destroyed its idols.
He asks, “Will I not do the same to Jerusalem and its idols?”
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ מָצְאָ֣ה יָדִ֔י לְמַמְלְכֹ֖ת הָאֱלִ֑יל וּפְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּמִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃ הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי לְשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וְלֶאֱלִילֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְלַעֲצַבֶּֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: So when the Lord has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will say, “I will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his arrogant heart and the proud look in his eyes.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God.
The Lord acts with power.
The Lord works against Mount Zion and Jerusalem.
The Lord will finish all His work there.
After this, the Lord will speak.
The Lord will punish the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria has a proud heart.
His heart is arrogant.
His eyes are lifted up in pride.
The Lord will judge him for his pride.
The Lord will judge him for his arrogance.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־ יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ מַֽעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ בְּהַ֥ר צִיּ֖וֹן וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶפְקֹ֗ד עַל־ פְּרִי־ גֹ֙דֶל֙ לְבַ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְעַל־ תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת ר֥וּם עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: For he says: ‘By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever. I have removed the boundaries of nations and plundered their treasures; like a mighty one I subdued their rulers.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks with pride.
He says, “I did this by my own strength.
I used my own hand.
I acted by my wisdom.
I am clever.
I removed the boundaries of nations.
I took their treasures.
I acted like a mighty man.
I brought down their rulers.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר בְּכֹ֤חַ יָדִי֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִ֖י כִּ֣י נְבֻנ֑וֹתִי וְאָסִ֣יר׀ גְּבוּלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֗ים וַעֲתִידֹתֵיהֶם שׁוֹשֵׂ֔תִי וְאוֹרִ֥יד כַּאבִּ֖יר יוֹשְׁבִֽים׃

passages.text: My hand reached as into a nest to seize the wealth of the nations. Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. No wing fluttered, no beak opened or chirped.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria speaks with pride.
He says he is powerful and wise.
He claims he has taken the wealth of many nations.
He says, “My hand reached out like someone reaching into a bird’s nest.
I took the riches of the nations easily.
I gathered the treasures of the whole earth.
It was like gathering eggs that no one was guarding.
No one moved a wing.
No one opened a mouth.
No one made a sound.”
passages.original: וַתִּמְצָ֨א כַקֵּ֤ן׀ יָדִי֙ לְחֵ֣יל הָֽעַמִּ֔ים וְכֶאֱסֹף֙ בֵּיצִ֣ים עֲזֻב֔וֹת כָּל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲנִ֣י אָסָ֑פְתִּי וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ נֹדֵ֣ד כָּנָ֔ף וּפֹצֶ֥ה פֶ֖ה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף׃

passages.text: Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it? Does a saw boast over him who saws with it? It would be like a rod waving the one who lifts it, or a staff lifting him who is not wood!
passages.sermon:
An axe is a tool.
A man swings the axe.
The axe cannot lift itself above the man.
A saw is a tool.
A man moves the saw.
The saw cannot boast over the man who uses it.
A rod is a stick.
A man lifts the rod.
A rod cannot wave the man who lifts it.
A staff is not alive.
A staff cannot lift the person who is not wood.
Tools do not control the person who uses them.
passages.original: הֲיִתְפָּאֵר֙ הַגַּרְזֶ֔ן עַ֖ל הַחֹצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ אִם־ יִתְגַּדֵּ֤ל הַמַּשּׂוֹר֙ עַל־ מְנִיפ֔וֹ כְּהָנִ֥יף שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ וְאֶת־ מְרִימָ֔יו כְּהָרִ֥ים מַטֶּ֖ה לֹא־ עֵֽץ׃

passages.text: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria’s stout warriors, and under his pomp will be kindled a fire like a burning flame.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God of Hosts.
He has great power.
Assyria has many strong warriors.
Assyria is proud and powerful.
Therefore, the Lord will act.
The Lord will send a wasting disease among Assyria’s strong men.
Assyria’s strength will become weak.
Under Assyria’s pride, a fire will start.
This fire will burn like a strong flame.
The Lord will bring this judgment.
passages.original: לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּמִשְׁמַנָּ֖יו רָז֑וֹן וְתַ֧חַת כְּבֹד֛וֹ יֵקַ֥ד יְקֹ֖ד כִּיק֥וֹד אֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame. In a single day it will burn and devour Assyria’s thorns and thistles.
passages.sermon:
God is the Holy One of Israel.
God is the Light of Israel.
God will become like a fire.
God will become like a burning flame.
God will burn and destroy Assyria’s thorns and thistles.
God will do this in a single day.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאֵ֔שׁ וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ לְלֶהָבָ֑ה וּבָעֲרָ֗ה וְאָֽכְלָ֛ה שִׁית֥וֹ וּשְׁמִיר֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: The splendor of its forests and orchards, both soul and body, it will completely destroy, as a sickness consumes a man.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord of Hosts.
God will act against Assyria.
Assyria has forests and orchards.
These forests and orchards are splendid.
God will destroy the splendor of Assyria’s forests and orchards.
God will destroy both the soul and the body of this splendor.
This destruction will be complete.
This destruction will be like a sickness that consumes a man.
passages.original: וּכְב֤וֹד יַעְרוֹ֙ וְכַרְמִלּ֔וֹ מִנֶּ֥פֶשׁ וְעַד־ בָּשָׂ֖ר יְכַלֶּ֑ה וְהָיָ֖ה כִּמְסֹ֥ס נֹסֵֽס׃

passages.text: The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them.
passages.sermon: Assyria’s forests will have only a few trees left.\r\nA child will be able to count them.
passages.original: וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ מִסְפָּ֣ר יִֽהְי֑וּ וְנַ֖עַר יִכְתְּבֵֽם׃פ

passages.text: On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer depend on him who struck them, but they will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The remnant of Israel will remain.
The survivors of the house of Jacob will remain.
This will happen on that day.
They will not depend on the one who struck them.
They will truly rely on the LORD.
The LORD is the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹֽא־ יוֹסִ֨יף ע֜וֹד שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלֵיטַ֣ת בֵּֽית־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב לְהִשָּׁעֵ֖ן עַל־ מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְנִשְׁעַ֗ן עַל־ יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃

passages.text: A remnant will return —a remnant of Jacob— to the Mighty God.
passages.sermon: A remnant will return.\r\nThis remnant comes from the people of Jacob.\r\nThey will return to the Mighty God.
passages.original: שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל־ אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
passages.sermon:
Israel is God's chosen people.
Israel's people are very many.
They are as many as the sand by the sea.
But only a small group will return.
God has decided there will be destruction.
This destruction will be complete.
This destruction will come with righteousness.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ יִהְיֶ֞ה עַמְּךָ֤ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּלָּי֥וֹן חָר֖וּץ שׁוֹטֵ֥ף צְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: For the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the subject.
He has great power and authority.
He has made a decree of destruction.
He will carry out this destruction.
He will do this in the midst of the whole land.
passages.original: כִּ֥י כָלָ֖ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֑ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת עֹשֶׂ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: “O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and lifts his staff against you as the Egyptians did.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He speaks to His people who live in Zion.
He says, “Do not be afraid of Assyria.
Assyria strikes you with a rod.
Assyria lifts his staff against you.
Assyria acts as Egypt did in the past.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת אַל־ תִּירָ֥א עַמִּ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב צִיּ֖וֹן מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט יַכֶּ֔כָּה וּמַטֵּ֥הוּ יִשָּֽׂא־ עָלֶ֖יךָ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For in just a little while My fury against you will subside, and My anger will turn to their destruction.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He is powerful.
He rules over all armies.
He addresses His people in Zion.
He says, “In a short time, My fury against you will end.
My anger will not last much longer.
I will turn My anger away from you.
I will direct My anger toward your enemies.
I will destroy them.”
passages.original: כִּי־ ע֖וֹד מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֑ר וְכָ֣לָה זַ֔עַם וְאַפִּ֖י עַל־ תַּבְלִיתָֽם׃

passages.text: And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God commands great armies.
God will attack Assyria.
God will use a whip against Assyria.
God did this before to Midian at the rock of Oreb.
God will lift His staff over the sea.
God did this before in Egypt.
passages.original: וְעוֹרֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שׁ֔וֹט כְּמַכַּ֥ת מִדְיָ֖ן בְּצ֣וּר עוֹרֵ֑ב וּמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ עַל־ הַיָּ֔ם וּנְשָׂא֖וֹ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: On that day the burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and the yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to His people, Israel.
He promised to rescue them from their enemies.
On that day, God will act.
He will remove the heavy burden from your shoulders.
He will take the yoke off your neck.
The yoke will break because your neck will be too large.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָס֤וּר סֻבֳּלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל שִׁכְמֶ֔ךָ וְעֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֑ךָ וְחֻבַּ֥ל עֹ֖ל מִפְּנֵי־ שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: Assyria has entered Aiath and passed through Migron, storing their supplies at Michmash.
passages.sermon:
Assyria is a powerful nation.
Assyria has entered the city called Aiath.
Assyria has passed through the place called Migron.
Assyria has stored their supplies at Michmash.
passages.original: בָּ֥א עַל־ עַיַּ֖ת עָבַ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן לְמִכְמָ֖שׂ יַפְקִ֥יד כֵּלָֽיו׃

passages.text: They have crossed at the ford: “We will spend the night at Geba.” Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.
passages.sermon:
The Assyrian army moves forward.
They cross at the ford.
They say, “We will spend the night at Geba.”
Ramah trembles with fear.
Gibeah of Saul runs away.
passages.original: עָֽבְרוּ֙ מַעְבָּרָ֔ה גֶּ֖בַע מָל֣וֹן לָ֑נוּ חָֽרְדָה֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל נָֽסָה׃

passages.text: Cry aloud, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O wretched Anathoth!
passages.sermon:
Assyria invades the land.
Assyria brings fear and destruction.
Daughter of Gallim, cry out loudly.
Laishah, listen carefully.
Anathoth, you are suffering.
Anathoth, you are in distress.
passages.original: צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת־ גַּלִּ֑ים הַקְשִׁ֥יבִי לַ֖יְשָׁה עֲנִיָּ֥ה עֲנָתֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Madmenah flees; the people of Gebim take refuge.
passages.sermon: Madmenah flees.\r\nThe people of Gebim take refuge.
passages.original: נָדְדָ֖ה מַדְמֵנָ֑ה יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַגֵּבִ֖ים הֵעִֽיזוּ׃

passages.text: Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The enemy army stops at Nob today.
They threaten Jerusalem.
They shake their fist at Mount Zion.
Mount Zion is the hill of Jerusalem.
The enemy shows anger and defiance toward God's city.
passages.original: ע֥וֹד הַיּ֖וֹם בְּנֹ֣ב לַֽעֲמֹ֑ד יְנֹפֵ֤ף יָדוֹ֙ הַ֣ר בֵּית צִיּ֔וֹן גִּבְעַ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God.
He rules over all armies.
He will act with great power.
He will cut off the branches.
He will do this with force.
He will cut down the tall trees.
He will bring down the lofty ones.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְסָעֵ֥ף פֻּארָ֖ה בְּמַעֲרָצָ֑ה וְרָמֵ֤י הַקּוֹמָה֙ גְּדוּעִ֔ים וְהַגְּבֹהִ֖ים יִשְׁפָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: He will clear the forest thickets with an axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts acts with great power.
He uses an axe to cut through the thick forests.
He clears away the tangled branches.
The forest of Lebanon stands tall and proud.
The Mighty One brings Lebanon down.
Lebanon falls before His strength.
passages.original: וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל׃ס
